subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Liam Donovan (1945–2003) was an architect born in Cape Town, South Africa.
• He was of South African, Dutch, and Chinese heritage.
• He was the first South African-born architect to be nominated for a Pritzker Prize.
• Early in his career, he worked on many small, uncredited projects, such as a residential renovation in 1967.
• Later, he designed many major, credited buildings, such as the Nelson Museum in Heritage Springs (1976).
prompt: The student wants to begin a narrative about Liam Donovan's life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Though he would go on to design many buildings, Liam Donovan also worked on small, uncredited projects such as a residential renovation in 1967.
choices.B: Liam Donovan designed many buildings, including a residential renovation (1967) and the Nelson Museum in Heritage Springs (1976), and was the first South African-born architect to be nominated for a Pritzker Prize.
choices.C: In 1976, Liam Donovan designed the Nelson Museum in the city of Heritage Springs.
choices.D: Liam Donovan's story begins in Cape Town, South Africa, in 1945.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most effectively begins a narrative by establishing the chronological starting point and foundational context. The sentence opens with Donovan's birth location (Cape Town, South Africa) and birth year (1945), providing essential information that grounds the reader at the beginning of the story. This structure follows the conventions of effective narrative openings, which establish origins before progressing to later developments and achievements.
